key_insight: A hybrid photon-atom architecture can combine photonic long-range connectivity with atomic near-deterministic control to make fault-tolerant quantum computing more hardware-efficient.
engineering_relevance: The design offers a practical route to scalable fault-tolerant quantum hardware by reducing photonic overhead while supporting cluster-state generation, entangling gates, and error correction in realistic cavity-QED systems.
method: Use single 87Rb atoms in optical cavities as reusable sources for photon generation and photon-atom entangling operations.
Implement a symmetrized Duan-Kimble controlled-phase gate to create high-fidelity, near-deterministic photon-atom CZ interactions.
Build large RHG cluster states with measurement-based quantum computing and analyze performance under asymmetric loss and correlated noise.
evidence_signal: Abstract-level simulations report a photon-loss threshold near 2.6% per physical gate, corresponding to about 15% total loss per trajectory, with Clifford operations matching identity-channel thresholds.
watch_item: The architecture depends on precise cavity-QED control and stringent loss/noise management, so experimental asymmetries and correlated errors may constrain real-world performance.
paper_title: Blueprint for a fault-tolerant compound photon-atom quantum architecture
